 U.K. Royals Charles left without umbrella in rainstorm fit for a king
 As the rain hammered down on King ​Charles he was seen gesturing to ⁠try to attract the attention of someone who might help, while his wife was shielded from the downpour. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 King Charles at an Independence Day parade during a heavy downpour in Antigua on Sunday. Matias Delacroix / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 2, 2026, 7:24 AM EST  /  Updated   Nov. 2, 2026, 8:37 AM EST / Source : Reuters By Reuters SAINT GEORGE, Antigua and Barbuda — King Charles flung up his hands in despair as he was caught in a tropical rainstorm in ​Antigua, while his wife Queen Camilla strolled off with the ‌only available umbrella.
 The couple’s Caribbean tour has been dominated by the debate over Britain’s role in the slave trade, but it was the sight of the soaked monarch ​which made headlines this weekend.
 As the rain hammered down on ​Charles, 77, he was seen gesturing and turning round to ⁠try to attract the attention of someone who might help, while Camilla ​was shielded from the downpour.
 00:32 King Charles caught without umbrella in rainstorm
 00:00 00:00 Locals taking part in the Antigua and Barbuda ​independence day parade did not flinch as they were lashed by the storm.
 Charles was eventually given an umbrella and was seen joking about his experience with Prime ​Minister Gaston Browne. “I think I’m about to grow watercress on my suit,” ​he said in a video posted on the royal family’s Instagram account.
 It is not ‌the ⁠first time the frustration of the famously short-fused monarch has been captured in public.
 Not long after he became king in 2022 in an incident which went viral on social media, he reacted grumpily when a pen ​leaked ink onto ​his hand at ⁠an event in Northern Ireland.
 “Oh God, I hate this,” he cursed. “I can’t bear this bloody thing... every stinking ​time,” he continued.
 He has since made fun of himself, ​quipping ⁠at a subsequent event, “I’m hoping that my pen is going to work. It doesn’t usually.”
 He is due to make a speech to Commonwealth leaders on ⁠Tuesday. ​Since becoming king, he has expressed sorrow ​for the suffering caused by slavery without crossing a line that Britain has long resisted: an ​apology.
